weighted_total_basis: capability as evidenced in professional-journey.md and the killer-query case studies only; open claims and résumé-only wording are named and left out. No résumé is tailored for this seat: his Naukri profile is what went forward (his call), so there is no résumé-surface score.
jd_source: jd.md below its marked line: the LinkedIn posting he found (linkedin.com/jobs/view/4466271472). Nielsen sent no job description; that this posting is the role the recruiter called about is his reading, not confirmed.
honest_ceiling_basis: What-if only: if professional-journey.md came to carry the résumé-only items (the Jenkins to GitHub Actions move and the Puppeteer suite; Elastic Container Service Fargate and Terraform; high availability), the containers, CI/CD, cloud and distributed-systems rows would rise by about 1.7 points together. 95 is not reachable honestly: test-driven development, Domain-Driven Design, the Lambda and Kappa names, cross-service distributed tracing and data pipelines proven at catalogue scale are absent from every source. Kubernetes stays out of the ceiling because it is open.
binding_constraint: The job description names five delivery-and-operations practices that professional-journey.md never names: test-driven development (TDD), a CI/CD tool, Kubernetes, distributed tracing and FinOps. The work beside each is real and cited (automated regression and replay tests, with CI on the production call path; Docker Compose and Elastic Container Service; Datadog and production tracing of the model pipeline; cost-driven consolidation and vendor replacement), so each scores as a partial, not a zero. The four rows that carry them lose 5.51 of the 13.61 points lost. Kubernetes is open (his August 2026 confirmation against the interview-prep ledger) and is scored on the journey alone. Second: data architecture (8.5), where the constructs are strong but the proven volume is a ~10,000-patient platform, not a catalogue.
smallest_honest_lift: No new claim; the application has gone, so the lift is how he names work already in the record when Nielsen talks to him. (1) Data engineering in the job description's words: the killer-query platform runs a live projection and a nightly batch lane side by side, replays nine years of history through the same projection code as the live stream ('the same projection code serves history and live'; one Kappa-like part of a hybrid design, and he should not call it Kappa himself), keeps event time apart from ingestion time with a watermark, and makes the historical load 'idempotent and resumable', quarantining rows it cannot map (kq1:289-290, 345-348, 381-400; kq4:711-713). (2) Automated testing, said as exactly that and never as TDD: golden-replay regression fixtures, CI on the production call path with a mock provider, and tenant isolation enforced by automated tests (kq4:849-851; kq1:753-754; journey 599). (3) A metadata-matching story for a metadata business: supplier hotel codes reconciled onto licensed GIATA MultiCodes, automated on AWS Lambda with the approval step kept human (journey 437-438, 446). Before the call, two things only he can settle: Kubernetes (his August 2026 confirmation against the prep ledger; the master résumé's headline names it, so it may come up), and, if message brokers come up, that his is Amazon Kinesis, since Kafka is on the prep ledger's never-claim list.
